info.title: Food Ordering Platform — client API
info.description:
Every client-facing endpoint routed by the API gateway (http://localhost:8080). Services communicate with each other only through RabbitMQ events, which are documented in API.md / ARCHITECTURE.md §16.3, not here.

**Authentication:** log in with `POST /auth/login`, then click **Authorize** and paste the `accessToken`. Each operation lists the roles allowed (`x-roles`).

**Money** is always integer paise. **Envelope:** `{ "success": true, "data": … , "meta"? }` or `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`. Every response has an `x-request-id` header.

Not described (internal only): the Notification Service, RabbitMQ, MongoDB and the per-service ports.

patch.description: **Roles: `platform_admin`.** Deactivating an active account publishes `auth.user.deactivated.v1` (transactional outbox); the Catalog Service then removes the user from every restaurant's adminIds (eventual consistency). Deactivating an inactive account publishes nothing. Reactivation restores login only — restaurant assignments are **not** restored. The Delivery Service also blocks a deactivated agent from new assignments until they sign in again after reactivation. You cannot deactivate yourself, and the last active platform administrator cannot be deactivated (concurrent deactivations are serialized).

delete.description: **Roles: `platform_admin`.** Deletes the Auth record of an **inactive** account and, in the same transaction, writes `auth.user.deleted.v1` to the outbox. Catalog then removes the id from every restaurant's adminIds and refuses to assign it again; Delivery blocks a deleted agent. Orders, payments, invoices, ledger entries and delivery history are kept and may still contain the user id and the name/email/address captured at the time. Ids are never reused. A JWT already issued to the user stays cryptographically valid until it expires (≤ 1 h). A repeated request returns 404 and publishes nothing.

get.description: **Roles: `customer`, `restaurant_admin`, `delivery_agent`, `platform_admin`.** Owner, the restaurant's admin, the **assigned** delivery partner, or a platform admin; anyone else gets 404. `text/event-stream`: a snapshot on connect, then `event: tracking` per committed change (`id` = history length), `: ping` heartbeats every 15 s and `event: end` once the order is settled (e.g. a cancelled order streams until its refund lands). The token must be in the Authorization header (Swagger UI cannot render streams; use curl -N or the testing console).
